title: Streamlined JSONL Sidecar: Timestamp Canonicalizer + Loki Bulk Writer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight JSONL sidecar that canonicalizes event timestamps, normalizes tenant and service labels, generates idempotency tokens for dedup, and writes to Loki via a bulk/optimized path. This component addresses skewed client clocks and inconsistent event_time fields while preserving ingest ordering and offering adaptive batching to meet latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar accepts newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) over HTTP/Unix socket and validates schema against known structured-log profile
Event timestamp normalization: prefer event_time field, fall back to server_time, and attach a canonical_iso8601 timestamp; preserve original fields

Clock skew correction: if event_time is more than 5 minutes ahead of server_time, mark record with metadata 'future_event=true' and correct timestamp to server_time; provide metric for corrected_count
Idempotency tokens generated for producer_id + sequence or provided idempotency_key; downstream Loki writes are deduplicated for exactly-once semantics per 10s window
Bulk writes to Loki reduce per-event overhead: throughput improvement of >=2x in benchmark vs current single-event push
Backpressure behaviour: when Loki is slow, sidecar applies adaptive flush thresholds and returns 429 with Retry-After; no unbounded memory growth
End-to-end tests and perf harness demonstrate <120ms p95 additional latency at 5k events/s with 8MB batching limit
Observability: expose Prometheus metrics (ingest_total, corrected_count, dedup_hits, flush_latency_seconds) and structured logs for errors
Rollout plan validated via canary on non-prod org and toggled via feature flag
implementation_notes: Rust sidecar binary using serde_json & tokio; schema validation via compiled JSON Schema; idempotency store backed by a compact LRU memtable with optional RocksDB persistence for Private deployments. Loki bulk writer uses /loki/api/v1/push with batched streams and label normalization. Provide feature flags: sidecar.dedupe_enabled, sidecar.max_batch_bytes, sidecar.skew_threshold_ms.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete - prototype normalizes timestamps and writes small batches to a local Loki instance (repo: github.com/redwood/in-perf/sidecar-spike)
2026-03-05: Design review with Observability leads - approved timestamp-correction heuristics; asked to add explicit 'original_event_time' field instead of overwriting
2026-03-08: Implemented idempotency token generation and LRU memtable; unit tests for token collision edge cases added
2026-03-10: Perf run on m5.4xlarge: 5k events/s with 4MB batch config achieved ~2.3x less CPU per event versus current per-event proxy
2026-03-12: Security review kickoff scheduled; adding KMS integration for private deployment dedupe seed persistence as action item
risks: Large tenants with high fanout could hit memory pressure for dedupe store; mitigation: bounded persistent cache and eviction policy
Incorrect timestamp correction could hide root cause of producer clock drift; mitigation: surface corrected_count metric and sample affected records to BigQuery
Added latency from batch flush may impact low-latency traces; mitigation: adaptive flush by age and size and per-route config
testing_plan: Unit tests for timestamp selection logic and future_event flag
Integration tests with a live Loki cluster running in CI with failure injection (timeouts, partial writes)
Perf tests using k6 + synthetic producers to validate flush thresholds at 1k/5k/20k events/s
Chaos tests that simulate clock skew and out-of-order ingestion to validate dedupe correctness
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deploy to staging-only for 48h with synthetic load
Canary to 5% of production orgs for 72h with verbose telemetry
Monitor corrected_count, dedup_hits, flush_latency, and error_rate; rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or corrected_count spikes 10x baseline
Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days with ops runbook for manual rollback
